title: WARDOGS: helicopter HUD and default HOTAS

sources.title: WARDOGS helicopters: controls, flight assist and unlock costs

intro: WARDOGS is a multiplayer combat game in which players also fly helicopters. All its helicopters share one simple control layout: the stick is the cyclic, the throttle lever is the collective, and the flight information is drawn on a HUD over the view. This guide explains the HUD, the instrument panel and the joystick layout.

areas.name: Game HUD
areas.text: The flight information over the view.

panels.name: Game HUD
panels.text: WARDOGS draws its flight information over the view instead of on cockpit instruments: height, speed, the weapon and its ammunition, the flares left and the lock state.
panels.context: The pilot reads it all the time; it is the same in every WARDOGS helicopter.

controls.name: Altitude
controls.text: Shows how high the helicopter is above the ground below it.
controls.context: Flying low keeps the helicopter hidden behind hills and buildings, but leaves little room for mistakes.

controls.name: Speed
controls.text: Shows how fast the helicopter moves through the air.
controls.context: The pilot slows down to land or drop off the squad, and speeds up to cross open ground.

controls.name: Weapon and ammunition
controls.text: Shows the selected weapon and how many rounds or rockets are left.
controls.context: When it runs low the pilot reloads with the reload button or goes back to rearm.

controls.name: Flares
controls.text: Shows how many flares are left. Flares are hot burning decoys that fool heat-seeking missiles.
controls.context: The pilot fires them with the thumb button when a missile comes.

controls.name: Lock state
controls.text: Shows the state of the target lock, which the pilot steps through with the Cycle Lock State button.
controls.context: Weapons that need a lock fire at the locked target.

areas.name: Instrument panel
areas.text: The instruments in front of the pilot.

panels.name: Instrument panel
panels.text: The instruments in front of the pilot: the collective position, the rotor state and the basic flight instruments.
panels.context: The game's HUD shows most of the same facts; the panel is there to look at in the cockpit view.

controls.name: Collective gauge
controls.text: Shows where the collective lever is set, which decides how hard the rotor lifts.
controls.context: Helpful with a joystick throttle that has no clear middle: the gauge shows where the lever really is.

controls.name: Rotor state
controls.text: Shows whether the rotor is running or still spinning up.
controls.context: The helicopter can only lift off once the rotor runs at full speed.

controls.name: Flight instruments
controls.text: Dials for speed, height and attitude (whether the nose is up or down and the rotor level).
controls.context: They help in the cockpit view when the pilot does not look at the HUD.

areas.name: Cyclic and collective
areas.text: The joystick layout every WARDOGS helicopter shares.

panels.name: Cyclic (stick)
panels.text: The joystick is the cyclic: the stick that tilts the rotor to fly forward, back and sideways. Its buttons fire, drop flares, lock targets and reload.
panels.context: WARDOGS binds the stick's axes by default but leaves its buttons free; the player assigns them in the joystick settings.

controls.name: Cyclic (stick axes)
controls.text: Forward and back pitch the nose down and up, sideways rolls the helicopter. The stick sets how fast it turns, not a fixed angle. Twisting the stick turns the nose left and right (yaw).
controls.context: By default X is roll, Y is pitch and the twist axis is yaw.

controls.name: Trigger (fire)
controls.text: Fires the helicopter's weapon. It is not bound by default; the player sets it in the joystick settings.
controls.context: What it fires depends on the helicopter; the unarmed transports have nothing to fire.

controls.name: Thumb button (flares)
controls.text: Fires flares, hot burning decoys that pull heat-seeking missiles away from the helicopter.
controls.context: The pilot fires them as soon as a missile warning comes; the HUD shows how many are left.

controls.name: Second thumb button (cycle lock state)
controls.text: Steps through the target lock states, for example to lock a target for the weapons.
controls.context: The lock state shows on the HUD.

controls.name: Third thumb button (reload)
controls.text: Reloads the weapon with the ammunition the helicopter carries.
controls.context: The ammunition count on the HUD shows when a reload is needed.

controls.name: Hat switch (look around)
controls.text: Turns the pilot's view up, down, left and right.
controls.context: Looking around helps to find the landing zone and threats beside the helicopter.

panels.name: Collective (throttle)
panels.text: The throttle lever works as the collective, the lever that makes the helicopter climb or sink. Its buttons hold voice chat, the map and the camera.
panels.context: By default the collective is the joystick's Z axis, the throttle wheel or lever on most stick bases.

controls.name: Collective
controls.text: Pushing the lever up makes the rotor lift harder so the helicopter climbs; pulling it down makes it sink.
controls.context: The pilot uses it with the cyclic: more lift to climb out of a landing zone, less to come down on it.

controls.name: Throttle button (voice push-to-talk)
controls.text: While held, the player's microphone sends voice to the team.
controls.context: Talking to the squad in the back is how the pilot coordinates drop-offs.

controls.name: Second throttle button (tactical map)
controls.text: Opens the tactical map with the battlefield and the objectives.
controls.context: The pilot plans the route to the next landing zone on it.

controls.name: Third throttle button (camera mode)
controls.text: Switches the camera mode, for example between the cockpit view and an outside view.
controls.context: An outside view helps to judge the space around the rotor when landing.
